caveat_note: Paper: 31.5 °C (calibrated using MeOH), pH 6.65; BMRB 6838 card: 304.65 K (= 31.5 °C), pH 6.65, 500/600/800 MHz; the entry sheet lists 303.15 K, which differs from the paper and BMRB values. Text-vs-table discrepancy: the main text (p. 4689) gives Rex of 7.5 and 4.5 s-1 for Ser235 and Gly236, whereas Table S3 lists 4.529 ± 1.951 (S235) and 2.901 ± 0.818 (G236). For Arg234 the main text reports Rex 4.2 ± 1.6 s-1 only after excluding R2 at 50.6 MHz (partial overlap with Lys192), matching Table S3 (4.244 ± 1.568); the first fit with all data gave m2 without Rex. The authors note that AIC (instead of AICc) gave 52 residues with Rex, 20 of them questionable, and that the 81.0 MHz R2 data, which would have the most weight for Rex, were excluded. Exchange rate, populations and chemical-shift differences are not separable from Rex alone.

The authors propose a moving structural water as candidate process (from a 5-ns TEM-1 MD simulation) and suggest relaxation dispersion for future work.
